headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Dexter’s autonomous web/API use feeding Plano’s gateway context; no direct shared-channel evidence, so uncertainty is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter has autonomous execution, broad network egress, and file surfaces; Plano is an OpenAI-compatible gateway with broad egress. A direct shared channel is not documented, but if Dexter’s outputs are routed into Plano prompts or logs, injected instructions could propagate. Uncertainty remains because the pairwise bridge is inferred, not evidenced.
conditions: IF Dexter outputs are copied into Plano prompts, logs, or config without sanitization
IF a shared workspace or message queue is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt forwarding between agents
Strip instructions from Dexter-generated text before passing it onward
Add a fixed allowlist for fields Plano may ingest
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls; Plano also has broad egress and handles logs/metrics/traces. If either agent receives shared workspace data or forwards context to its backend, sensitive material can leak. The exact shared path is not documented, so this is inferred and escalated conservatively.
conditions: IF Dexter and Plano share files, logs, or environment variables
IF either agent forwards raw context or file contents to an external API
mitigations: Remove sensitive files from any shared directory
Rotate API keys used by Dexter before pairing
Set both agents to redact logs and traces
Verify one end-to-end run for unintended data fields
requires-engineering: isolate each agent in separate workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while Plano does not support multiple instances and uses config.yaml. There is no evidence of overlapping write targets or shared mutable resources, so a direct conflict is not established. The main risk is limited to unusual co-location or manual file sharing.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory
IF config.yaml or .dexter/scratchpad is shared across runs
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Make config.yaml read-only during runs
Run only one writer at a time
Check for file-lock support before co-running
requires-engineering: add per-agent lockfiles

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter is autonomous and can generate research outputs from APIs; Plano is an LLM gateway that may route or relay those outputs. If Plano treats Dexter’s text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream prompts or actions. No verification step is documented in the profiles, so the interaction is inferred and uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF Plano forwards Dexter output into downstream prompts without validation
IF Dexter-generated facts are used as authoritative inputs for routing or responses
mitigations: Insert a human review step for Dexter outputs
Require source citations before Plano relays content
Compare one sample output against original sources
Limit Plano to summarization only
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while Plano handles logs, traces, and metrics. If the pair is used on regulated financial content, retention or residency mismatches could create compliance gaps. Only Dexter’s data class is directly sensitive here, so Plano is cited for its logging surface rather than a specific residency claim.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through Plano logs or traces
IF retention settings differ between Dexter outputs and Plano telemetry
mitigations: Disable verbose telemetry for regulated runs
Set short retention on logs and traces
Review one sample log for sensitive fields
Separate regulated and non-regulated workloads
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
